concerns.text: FR-007 requires enforcing a hard timeout for the entire execution and analysis pipeline. Tasks T039 (Performance optimization) and T037 (Documentation) do not explicitly cover the implementation of the global timeout enforcement logic or the abort mechanism required by this functional requirement.

The spec's Edge Cases section mandates detecting network saturation (>20% packet loss) and aborting the run. Task T022 only implements the *injection* of latency/packet loss. There is no task explicitly implementing the *detection* and *abort* logic for this critical edge case.

SC-006 mandates that if critical variables (throughput, latency) are missing, the run is flagged as WARN and *excluded* from regression analysis. Task T032 describes flagging the run and proceeding with 'reduced model complexity,' which contradicts the exclusion requirement for critical missing data.

FR-005 requires quantifying interaction effects between heterogeneity and granularity. Task T027 (regression.py) and T028 (anova_test.py) do not explicitly mandate the implementation of specific interaction terms in the GAM model, risking a model that fails to validate the core hypothesis.

FR-006 requires validating scaling laws against theoretical bounds and flagging if empirical performance exceeds the limit. Tasks T029 (calculation) and T030 (comparison) are split; there is no single task explicitly defining the unified logic to 'flag if empirical performance exceeds the theoretical limit' as a validation step.

The spec requires measuring unmodeled variables (thermal throttling, OS noise) directly on real hardware for the 'Golden Dataset'. The plan and tasks (T033-T036) focus on simulation calibration but lack a specific task to capture these specific unmodeled variables in the physical data collection phase.
